title: Hardship Desk Q&A — Hold-Timing Extension of the Pre-Suspension Grace on Payment Arrangements
content:
For a plan under Payment Arrangements suspended for a hardship hold, the pre-suspension grace of the examined installment carries a hold-timing extension that follows when the hardship hold was asked for.

## Rule

The hold is the hardship hold that suspended the plan — the hold on the plan's account whose decision date is the plan's suspended date — as recorded under Hardship and Protective Holds, with its request date and its tier's documentation requirement.

- A hold of a tier that needs documentation, requested on or after the examined installment's scheduled due date and no more than 30 days after it, adds 2 days.
- A self-attested hold (a hold whose tier does not need documentation) requested on or after that date and no more than 30 days after it adds 1 day.
- Any other case, including a hold requested before that date, adds 0 days.

The days are calendar days from the scheduled due date to the request date: a request on the due date itself is 0 days after it, and a request 30 days after it is still inside the 30 days.

## Questions answered

**The installment was due on 1 May and a documented hold was requested on 31 May. Extension?**
31 May is 30 days after 1 May — no more than 30 — so 2 days. (Hypothetical dates.)

**The same documented hold requested on 1 June?**
31 days after the due date: 0 days.

**A self-attested hold requested on the due date itself?**
On or after the due date and within 30 days: 1 day.

**A hold of either kind requested on 28 April, before the 1 May due date?**
Requested before that date: 0 days.

## Summary

| Tier of the hold | Request date relative to the examined installment's due date | Extension |
|---|---|---|
| Needs documentation | From the due date to 30 days after | 2 days |
| Self-attested | From the due date to 30 days after | 1 day |
| Either | Before the due date, or more than 30 days after | 0 days |
